The account eSource@ENRON (40enron@enron.com) sent the most messages on 2001-09-05, with 23. It sent 160 messages in September 2001 in total. The next busiest days were 2001-09-28 with 19 and 2001-09-14 with 16.

SOURCES: E80e4adf85ec0

Angelic Davis (angelic.davis@enron.com) sent 6 unique messages to dana.davis@enron.com between 2001-10-01 and 2001-11-01 (end exclusive). I ran a metadata query on sender, recipient and date range, and it returned 6 distinct message ids. Dana Davis is on the To line of each one. Two of the six, Eec51ca95dc10 and Ea4671be47808, also went to a longer list of other recipients.

ANSWER: 6
SOURCES: Eec51ca95dc10, E78c208665714, Ea4671be47808, Ea9e43a0d11aa, Ef703ce92e611

Jeff Dasovich sent the most messages to Richard Sanders in that window. I found 37 messages sent to richard.sanders@enron.com (To or Cc) from 2001-05-29 up to but not including 2001-06-05, and 8 of them were from Dasovich. Susan Mara was next with 5, then Janette Elbertson with 4.

I counted by sender address across the 37 messages. The five source IDs below are some of Dasovich's 8.

ANSWER: jeff.dasovich@enron.com
SOURCES: Ec64a0fe2fe15, Efbeffae21bed, Eb4461cb03bfd, E89c6a95fd0e2, Eaa28b1519008

In April 2001 (UTC), Vince Kaminski sent the most messages to vkaminski@aol.com. That address appeared in To or Cc on 173 of his messages. I counted each message once per address.

I filtered to messages sent from vince.kaminski@enron.com that month, which gave 458. The next highest recipients were his own Enron address (135), shirley.crenshaw@enron.com (54) and vasant.shanbhogue@enron.com (36).

I didn't open individual messages, so I have no message ids to cite as sources.

ANSWER: vkaminski@aol.com
SOURCES:

The exact string "EB-2934" (with the hyphen) appears in only one message. The other eight matches are spelled "EB2934" with no hyphen, so I excluded them.

That message is E2093dccd9417, sent on 2000-12-05 with the subject "PSEG Meeting". Robin Barbe sent it to Chris Germany and Dick Jenkins. The matching line reads "50,000/d @ Transco Zone 6, on Tuesday, December 5, 3:00 p.m., in EB-2934." Here EB-2934 is a conference room, not a reference number.

ANSWER: robin.barbe@enron.com
SOURCES: E2093dccd9417

The reference ORE-7509 appears in exactly one message, **E2083b9620d07**. It was sent on 2002-02-27 and is titled "(CMS-26) NOTICE OF INTENTION TO TRANSFER MEMBERSHIP".

The sender was marketing@nymex.com, shown as "Exchange Information @ENRON". The message is in the deleted_items folder of custodian shackleton-s. The matching line reads "Edward Orenchuk (ORE-7509)", so the reference belongs to a person named in the notice.

ANSWER: marketing@nymex.com
SOURCES: E2083b9620d07
